title: Pro-etale closed support before constructible restriction
statement: Let $T$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]), let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be its open complement [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use the constant coefficient sheaves and small pro-etale sites with the size conventions of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The direct-image functor $i_*$ [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image], applied termwise to complexes, has a right adjoint. This right adjoint is the total right derived functor $Ri^!_0$ of the sheaf functor $i^!_0N=i^*\ker(N\to j_*j^*N)$ [def-exc-proetale-sections-with-support], where $i^*,j^*$ are the module inverse images [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. No constructibility or boundedness is imposed on objects or on the values of $Ri^!_0$.

proof.text: The open immersion is quasi-compact because its target is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Apply [lem-sf-ringed-closed-kernel-adjoint] to the actual constant ring sheaf. For the canonical constant-coefficient isomorphisms in [def-exc-proetale-sections-with-support], restriction along the coefficient isomorphism is an equivalence. Pushforward composition identifies the constant-coefficient direct image with this equivalence followed by the ringed direct image; uniqueness of left adjoints then identifies the two inverse images. The ringed theorem supplies the ordinary closed-support adjunction and exactness.

Evaluation preserves the functor-category kernel, giving the intrinsic sectionwise support kernel [def-exc-proetale-sections-with-support]. Composing an adjunction with a coefficient equivalence changes its unit target by the equivalence unit, which is invertible, and hence leaves its kernel naturally isomorphic. The left-adjoint comparison changes the right adjoint by its unique comparison and likewise transports the unit kernel. Whisker these kernel comparisons by closed inverse image to identify the intrinsic closed support functor with the ringed support functor followed by inverse coefficient equivalence. Transporting the ordinary adjunction of [lem-sf-ringed-closed-kernel-adjoint] yields the intrinsic sheaf adjunction. Exactness transports across the coefficient equivalence and direct-image comparison.

Apply the existing exact-left-adjoint unbounded derived-adjunction construction CategoryTheory.Adjunction.mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction to the transported sheaf adjunction. This implements the K-injective Hom argument of [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy], [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. The published module operations already provide K-injective resolutions, so no separate existence theorem is needed. Since closed direct image is exact, its total right derived functor is canonically its termwise mapDerivedCategory [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] (Functor.rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory, by uniqueness of derived functors). Transport the left adjoint along this isomorphism, obtaining exactly the displayed conjunction. No boundedness or constructibility restriction enters.
